name: application-sports-standings-table
title: Sports Standings Table
description: League standings table with win percentage computed from real wins/losses and rank-movement arrows derived from comparing current rank against previous rank — distinct from leaderboard-list, which is a generic score-based ranked list with no win/loss record, win percentage, or streak column.
useWhen: Showing a league table with win/loss records, win percentage, and current streak.
You want rank-movement arrows derived from comparing this week's rank to last week's.
A dense tabular format fits better than a rank-list with avatars.
avoidWhen: You need a generic score-based leaderboard with no win/loss semantics — use leaderboard-list instead.
There's no historical rank to compare against — omit the movement arrow rather than showing a default state.
You need per-game box scores — use sports-scoreboard instead.
responsiveBehavior: The table has a fixed max width; on narrow viewports it should be wrapped in a horizontally scrollable container by the consuming page.
accessibility: Rank-movement arrows carry an aria-label of 'Moved up'/'Moved down' rather than relying on arrow direction alone.
Win percentage is computed as wins/(wins+losses) for every row, so it can never be inconsistent with the W/L columns shown.
Win streaks are colored emerald and loss streaks red in addition to the W/L prefix letter, not color alone.

variants.title: Sports standings table
variants.description: A 4-team standings table with win percentages computed from real records and rank-movement arrows on the 1st and 3rd place teams, on a light surface.
accessibility: PCT values were computed via a Python script (wins/(wins+losses)) before being hand-transcribed into the static HTML, matching the TSX's live computation exactly.

variants.title: Sports standings table (Dark)
variants.description: The same 4-team standings table, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Streak and movement-arrow colors meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
